Most city Koreans live in 아파트 (apateu) — big high-rise complexes.
Our place is on the fifteenth floor.
층 (cheung) = floor, with Sino numbers: 십오 층 (sibo cheung = 15th floor).
I can see the mountains from home.
보여요 (boyeoyo) = 'is visible' — how Korean says I can see it.
The living room is very spacious.
거실 (geosil) = living room; 넓어요 (neolbeoyo) = is spacious.
개 (gae) = general counter, native numbers: 두 개 (du gae = two things).
The bathroom is a bit small.
There are lots of plant pots on the balcony.
베란다 (beranda) = balcony — where Koreans keep plants and laundry.
The people next door are kind.
옆집 (yeopjip) = the home next door: 옆 (next to) + 집 (house).
In the morning I open all the windows.
There's a park near my house.
The supermarket is close to home.
이사해요 (isahaeyo) = move house; 지난달 (jinandal) = last month.
The new place is really nice.
The monthly rent is a bit expensive.
I also pay the maintenance fee every month.
지하 (jiha) = underground — 지하철 is the 'underground train'!
The apartment playground is very big.
I clean the house every weekend.
Koreans 'spin' machines: 청소기를 돌려요 (cheongsogireul dollyeoyo = run the vacuum).
In the afternoon I ran the washing machine too.
빨래 (ppallae) = laundry: 빨래를 해요 = do the laundry.
설거지 (seolgeoji) = the dishes: 설거지를 해요 = wash the dishes.
I didn't do the dishes yesterday.
I tidied my room over the weekend.
I wipe the floor with a rag.
로 (ro) = with (a tool): 걸레로 (geollero = with a rag).
버려요 (beoryeoyo) = throw away: 쓰레기를 버려요 = take out the trash.
Cleaning the bathroom is really tough.
빨아요 (pparayo) = wash (fabric) — a special verb just for laundry!
I'll do the ironing in the afternoon.
물을 줘요 (mureul jwoyo) = 'give water' = to water plants.
Today we're doing a deep clean.
대청소 (daecheongso) = the big all-day clean; 대- (dae) = big.
My younger sibling helped with the cleaning.
Mom cooks and Dad does the dishes.
There's no milk in the fridge.
It was hot, so I turned on the AC.
켜요 (kyeoyo) = turn on: 에어컨을 켜요 = turn on the AC.
I turn off the lights before bed.
-기 전에 (gi jeone) = before doing: 자기 전에 (jagi jeone = before sleeping).
I didn't turn off the room light.
꺼요 (kkeoyo) = turn off, from 끄다 (kkeuda) — opposite of 켜요.
I closed the windows at night.
In Korea, people sort their recycling.
분리수거 (bullisugeo) = mandatory trash sorting — an apartment-life ritual.
Bottles and cans go out separately.
I threw out the food waste separately.
음식물 쓰레기 (eumsingmul sseuregi) = food waste — it gets its own bin in Korea.
I threw out all the cardboard boxes.
I'll do the recycling this evening.
배달 (baedal) = delivery — Korea's food-delivery culture is world-famous.
I ordered chicken on an app.
시켜요 (sikyeoyo) = order (food): 치킨을 시켜요 = order chicken.
벌써 (beolsseo) = already — sooner than you expected.
떡볶이 (tteokbokki) = spicy rice cakes — Korea's favorite street food.
On weekends we often eat delivery food.
Please leave it at the door.
문 앞에 놓아 주세요 (mun ape noa juseyo) — the delivery-app phrase.
